title: Chemical reactions and equations
summary: Learn about reactions, writing and balancing equations, what is conserved and the types of reactions.
cards.0.p: In a chemical reaction, substances turn into new substances. Gas given off, a change of color, a precipitate, heat or light are clues of a reaction. But they are not proof, because boiling water also gives off gas.
cards.0.key: The only sure test is whether a new substance forms.
cards.0.once.soru: Which one is a chemical reaction?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Iron and oxygen form a new substance, iron oxide.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Melted ice is still water. This is a change of state.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: When the water evaporates, the sugar is left behind. This is a physical change.
cards.1.p: In a reaction, bonds break, atoms rearrange and new bonds form. Atoms are not destroyed or created from nothing. In a physical change the substance keeps its identity. For example, melted ice is still water.
cards.1.key: In a reaction the atoms do not change. What changes is which atoms they are bonded to.
cards.2.p: In an equation, the reactants are written to the left of the arrow and the products to the right. The number in front of a formula is the coefficient. The state of a substance is shown as (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas or (aq) dissolved in water.
cards.2.key: A coefficient of 1 is not written. (l) means a pure liquid, and (aq) means a solution in water. For example, you write H₂O(l) but NaCl(aq).
cards.2.once.soru: In the equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, which side is water on?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: The substances to the right of the arrow are products, and they form in the reaction.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: The reactants are to the left of the arrow, and they are H₂ and O₂.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Water is written only to the right of the arrow, as a product.
cards.3.p: When balancing, you change only the coefficients. The subscripts decide what the substance is. If you change H2O to H2O2, you have turned water into hydrogen peroxide.
cards.3.key: 2H₂O means two water molecules. Coefficients should be the smallest whole numbers, as in 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
cards.4.p: The goal of balancing is to have the same number of each atom on both sides. Count the atoms and start with the most complex compound. Leave single elements such as O<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub> for last. If you get a fraction, multiply all the coefficients.
cards.4.etk.soru: Put the steps for balancing in the right order.
cards.4.svg#1: Write the formulas correctly; do not touch subscripts
cards.4.svg#3: Count each kind of atom separately on both sides
cards.4.svg#7: If there is a fraction, multiply; smallest whole numbers
cards.4.svg#9: Final check: is every atom equal on both sides?
cards.4.key: First write the formulas correctly, and at the end do a final check.
cards.5.p: The equation for burning ethane is C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. For C you write 2CO<sub>2</sub>, and for H 3H<sub>2</sub>O. There are 7 O on the right, so you need 7/2 O<sub>2</sub> on the left. Then all the coefficients are multiplied by 2.
cards.5.svg#17: Order: C, H, O last; when 7/2 appears, all × 2
cards.5.once.soru: When balancing C₂H₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O, what do you adjust first?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: First balance the atoms in compounds. Leave O₂, a single element, for last.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: O₂ is a single element. If you leave it for last, it is easy to adjust.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: Subscripts are never changed. Only coefficients are.
cards.6.p: In the equation Fe + O<sub>2</sub> → Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, oxygen comes in twos on the left and threes on the right, and the common multiple is 6. First write 3O<sub>2</sub> and 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, then add 4Fe on the left.
cards.6.svg#2: O: 2 on the left, 3 on the right
cards.6.svg#5: common multiple of 2 and 3 is 6: 6 O = 6 O
cards.6.svg#8: 2 × 2 = 4 Fe on the right → 4Fe on the left
cards.6.key: The result is 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. The (III) in the compound's name shows that iron has a +3 charge.
cards.6.once.soru: In the equation 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃, how many oxygen atoms are on the right?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: 2 × 3 = 6. The 3O₂ on the left also contains 6 O atoms.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The coefficient and the subscript are not added. They are multiplied.
cards.7.h: What is conserved in a reaction?
cards.7.p: In a reaction the nuclei do not change. Only electrons are rearranged. So the kinds and numbers of atoms, the mass and the charge are conserved. The number of molecules and the volume may not be.
cards.7.svg#11: 4 molecules → 2 molecules, but 2 N and 6 H on both sides
cards.7.key: In an ionic equation the charges must also balance. For example, in Zn + 2H⁺ → Zn²⁺ + H₂ the total charge on both sides is +2.
cards.7.once.soru: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, what is not conserved?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: 4 molecules go in, and 2 molecules come out.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: Mass is conserved in every reaction.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: There are 2 N and 6 H on both sides.
cards.8.p: Combustion is a substance reacting with oxygen and releasing heat. With enough oxygen, CO<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub>O form. As you just saw, with too little oxygen, CO and soot form too.
cards.8.svg#5: the products also include CO or soot (C)
cards.8.svg#6: ⚠ CO is colorless, odorless and toxic
cards.8.key: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and an ignition temperature. If any one is removed, burning stops. N₂ combines with oxygen by absorbing heat, so it is counted as not burning.
cards.9.p: In a synthesis reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product. If 1 mol of a compound forms from its elements, it is called a formation reaction. In a decomposition reaction, a compound breaks down into simpler substances.
cards.9.key: In synthesis several substances turn into one product. In decomposition one substance breaks into several products, and heat or electricity is often needed. ½N₂ + 3/2H₂ → NH₃ is a formation reaction.
cards.10.p: As you just saw, when two ionic solutions mix, some ions form a solid that does not dissolve. This solid is called a precipitate. Spectator ions are left out of the equation, as in Ag+ + Cl− → AgCl(s).
cards.10.svg#11: In the net equation, atoms and charge must balance too.
cards.10.key: The spectator ions here are Na⁺ and NO₃⁻. Salts of Na⁺, K⁺, NH₄⁺ and NO₃⁻ dissolve in water. AgCl, BaSO₄ and CaCO₃ dissolve only slightly.
cards.11.p: In an acid-base reaction, the H+ ion of the acid and the OH− ion of the base combine to form water. Usually a salt and water are produced. In redox reactions, electrons are exchanged.
cards.11.svg#5: Mg gives up electrons, O gains electrons.
cards.11.key: Both are covered in detail in their own topics. A reaction can belong to more than one type.
cards.11.once.soru: What type of reaction is HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: An acid and a base combine to form a salt and water. This is called neutralization.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: In decomposition a single compound breaks down. Here two substances react.
cards.12.p:
• In a reaction bonds break and form again, and a new substance forms.
• When balancing, only coefficients change, not subscripts.
• Atoms, mass and charge are conserved. The number of molecules can change.
• Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and an ignition temperature. Incomplete combustion forms CO.
• The types of reactions are combustion, synthesis, decomposition, acid-base, precipitation and redox.
cards.12.svg#1: atoms, mass and charge are conserved
quiz.0.q: When C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + a O<sub>2</sub> → b CO<sub>2</sub> + c H<sub>2</sub>O is balanced with the smallest whole numbers, what is a?
quiz.0.e: For C atoms b = 3, and for H atoms c = 4. There are 3·2 + 4 = 10 O atoms on the right. So a = 5.
quiz.1.q: In a chemical reaction in a closed container, which of these are conserved? Put each one in the right group.
quiz.1.e: In a reaction the nuclei do not change, and atoms are only rearranged. So the kinds and numbers of atoms, the mass and the charge are conserved. The number of molecules and the volume can change. For example, in N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>, 4 molecules form 2 molecules.
quiz.2.q: Match each reaction with its type.
quiz.2.e: Methane burns with oxygen. Nitrogen and hydrogen combine into a single product, so this is synthesis. The electrolysis of water is a compound breaking down, which is decomposition. Ag<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup> form a precipitate. HCl and NaOH give a salt and water, which is an acid-base reaction.
quiz.3.q: When BaCl₂ and Na₂SO₄ solutions are mixed, a white precipitate forms. What is the net ionic equation?
quiz.3.e: BaSO₄ dissolves only slightly in water, so it precipitates. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are spectator ions that stay unchanged on both sides, and they are not written in the net equation.
quiz.3.y.1: Na⁺ salts dissolve in water. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are spectator ions and do not form a precipitate.
quiz.3.y.2: This is the full equation. In the net equation the spectator ions are removed.
quiz.3.y.3: Na⁺ salts dissolve in water, so Na₂SO₄ does not precipitate.
A:ozet: Try it first, then learn its name. Rearrange atoms, balance an equation and see incomplete combustion.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Water will form from hydrogen and oxygen. First make a guess, then watch the atoms.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: What happens to the atoms during the reaction?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Atoms do not disappear. There were 4 H and 2 O before, and there are 4 H and 2 O after.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Bonds break, atoms rearrange and new bonds form. The atoms stay the same. Only what they are bonded to changes. So the number of atoms and the total mass are conserved.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: In a chemical reaction the nuclei do not change. Hydrogen stays hydrogen, and oxygen stays oxygen.
A:adimlar.1.metin: An equation must have the same number of each atom on both sides. This one has 2 O on the left and 1 O on the right.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: What is the right way to balance the oxygen?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The subscript decides what the substance is. H₂O₂ is not water but hydrogen peroxide. You would be writing a different substance.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Oxygen gas is made of O₂ molecules, and you cannot change its formula.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: Put a 2 in front of H₂O
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The coefficient shows the number of molecules, so 2H₂O means two water molecules. Only coefficients change, not subscripts.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Now set the coefficients yourself. In the equation H₂ + O₂ → H₂O, make every atom equal on both sides.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: The equation becomes 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, with 4 H and 2 O on both sides. Coefficients should be the smallest whole numbers. 4H₂ + 2O₂ → 4H₂O is also balanced, but it can be simplified.
A:adimlar.3.metin: When natural gas (methane) burns, CO₂ and water form. First balance C, then H. Leave O₂, a single element, for last.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: The equation becomes CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Both sides have 1 C, 4 H and 4 O. In a reaction the kinds and numbers of atoms, the mass and the charge are conserved. The number of molecules does not have to be.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Combustion is a substance reacting with oxygen. This stove is burning methane in a closed room with little air.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: What forms when methane burns without enough oxygen?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: That is complete combustion, and it needs enough oxygen.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The carbon in methane has to go somewhere too. It comes out as CO₂, CO or soot.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Incomplete combustion forms CO and soot (carbon). CO is colorless and odorless, and it binds to hemoglobin much more tightly than oxygen. That is why detectors and ventilation save lives.
A:adimlar.5.metin: When limestone is heated, quicklime and carbon dioxide form. To find the type of a reaction, look at the number of substances going in and coming out.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: What type of reaction is CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In synthesis several substances turn into one product. Here the opposite happens.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Here a compound breaks down into simpler substances, so several products form from one substance. Decomposition often needs heat or electricity, and here it needs heat.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Precipitation happens when two solutions mix. Here a single solid is heated.
A:adimlar.6.metin: When two ionic compounds dissolved in water are mixed, some ions can form a solid that does not dissolve in water. Silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions are both clear.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.soru: What happens when the divider is removed?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: A white solid settles to the bottom
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Ag⁺ and Cl⁻ combine to form AgCl, which does not dissolve in water, as a white precipitate. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ stay unchanged in the solution.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Some ion pairs do not dissolve in water. Which two of these ions could combine?
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: There is no ion pair here that could form a gas. The product is a solid.
A:kapanis.0: In a reaction, bonds break, atoms rearrange and new substances form.
A:kapanis.1: When balancing, only coefficients change, not subscripts. Coefficients should be the smallest whole numbers.
A:kapanis.2: The kinds and numbers of atoms, the mass and the charge are conserved. The number of molecules and the gas volume can change.
A:kapanis.3: Combustion happens with oxygen and releases heat. With too little oxygen, combustion is incomplete, and toxic CO and soot form.
A:kapanis.4: The types of reactions are combustion, synthesis, decomposition, precipitation, acid-base and redox. In synthesis substances combine, and in decomposition a substance breaks down.
